title: Firefly Aerospace Signs Rocket Engine Deal Valued at More Than $1.3 Billion with AST SpaceMobile
summary: Agreement supports AST SpaceMobile’s new heavy-lift rocket, while injecting additional funds for Firefly's launch vehicle production.
body_markdown:
**Firefly* *CEO Jason Kim and AST SpaceMobile Chairman and CEO Abel Avellan in front of Firefly’s Miranda engine at its Rocket Ranch in Briggs, Texas;* *Credit: Firefly Aerospace*


**CEDAR PARK, Texas** , **November 6, 2026** – Firefly Aerospace (Nasdaq: FLY), a market leading space and defense technology company, today announced an agreement with AST SpaceMobile (Nasdaq: ASTS) for more than $1.3 billion to deliver 36 rocket engines, provide a license to the engine’s intellectual property, and offer engineering support over a three-year period for[AST SpaceMobile’s new heavy-lift rocket](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261106165875/en/AST-SpaceMobile-to-Build-Own-20-Ton-Rocket-to-Deploy-BlueBird-Satellites-in-Low-Earth-Orbit-Using-Miranda-Engines-from-Firefly-Aerospace) . The agreement provides Firefly with additional funds to accelerate its existing launch vehicle production and broader technology roadmap.


Under the agreement, Firefly will deliver 27 of its Miranda engines and nine of its vacuum-variant Vira engines for AST SpaceMobile’s first three rockets, and provide the license for AST SpaceMobile to manufacture the engines.


“This is a bold transformational deal for Firefly, for AST SpaceMobile, and for the space industry,” said Jason Kim, CEO of Firefly Aerospace. “When a company sets out to build its own rocket, the engine is the hardest, highest-stakes decision they make, and AST SpaceMobile chose to partner with Firefly for its most powerful rocket engines. It’s a true win-win for both companies: AST SpaceMobile gets control of its own launch schedule, and Firefly gets added funds to rapidly expand our rocket production and reinforce the supply of launch vehicles to address record demand from the industry.”


Firefly’s Miranda engine has performed over 175 hot fire tests for more than 4,200 seconds, including a flight-like test at 110% performance of the 230,000 lbf thrust engine that successfully performed 20 seconds beyond the nominal flight duration of 206 seconds. Both Miranda and Vira utilize flight-proven technology scaled from the company’s Reaver and Lightning rocket engines, which were designed, built, and tested in-house with Firefly’s patented tap-off cycle technology and vertically integrated approach.


Both headquartered in Texas, Firefly and AST SpaceMobile have complementary business portfolios and missions, and the agreement is non-competitive by design. Firefly retains full ownership of its engine intellectual property and will continue to serve the broader government and commercial launch market.


“Firefly is one of a few companies in the United States with a proven liquid engine of this scale, making it a scarcity in the industry,” said Abel Avellan, Founder, Chairman and CEO of AST SpaceMobile. “We’re proud to partner with Firefly as a company that has demonstrated repeated launch success to orbit and completed the first and only successful commercial Moon landing.”


Under the terms of the agreements, AST SpaceMobile will pay Firefly more than $1.3 billion, consisting of cash and shares of AST Class A Common Stock with the latter subject to various lock-up periods.


The influx of funds allows Firefly to quickly expand hiring, procure long-lead materials, source optimal equipment, and fortify infrastructure, including multiple new test bays in Briggs, Texas, to increase its own launch vehicle production and testing. The added engineering capacity further allows Firefly to accelerate key milestones across its core programs and broader technology roadmap.


“The agreement supercharges Firefly’s production system — more test bays at our Rocket Ranch, long-lead materials bought ahead, and a bigger team of engineers and technicians,” said Kim. “This allows us to build and test faster across our launch portfolio, with safety, quality, and reliability built in.”


**Investor Presentation and Webcast on November 10**


For additional information, Firefly will discuss this agreement during our upcoming[Third Quarter 2026 Earnings call](https://investors.fireflyspace.com/events/event-details/firefly-aerospace-third-quarter-2026-financial-results-conference-call) scheduled for 5 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

**About Firefly Aerospace**


Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company on a mission to reliably and repeatedly launch, land, and operate space systems from Earth to the Moon and beyond. As the partner of choice for responsive space missions, Firefly is the first commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with approximately 24-hour notice and the first to achieve a successful Moon landing. Firefly’s launch, lunar, and orbital vehicles paired with its AI software and data processing capabilities support end-to-end missions across cislunar space, including payload delivery and maneuverability, space domain awareness, and missile warning and tracking. Established in 2017, Firefly’s engineering, manufacturing, and test facilities are co-located in central Texas to enable rapid innovation and vertical integration across the company’s product lines. For more information, visit[www.fireflyspace.com](http://www.fireflyspace.com/) .
